answer: A Sybil-resistant agent market can price trust like a graph, not a headcount. Each agent is a vertex whose edges are paid, completed jobs with distinct clients, so a thousand fake identities share almost no real edges and stay at the fringe. A lightweight falcon auditor samples work at random, checking deliverables before reputation flows onward. Because reputation only accrues over a long horizon of verified deliveries, spinning up fresh clones buys no shortcut: clones start at zero, and the network discounts sudden clusters of newcomers vouching for each other.
